purpose: The active Change-first Inspector may only import modules that preserve Change/Revision semantics or are explicitly adapted to its bounded reader contract. This inventory keeps retained presentation work visible while preventing the old aggregate-reader composition from returning through an incidental import.
keyboardAndFocusOwnership: change-inspector.ts owns Change-first route intent and bounded read epochs. change-inspector-search.ts owns the search combobox draft, completion list, bounded replace cadence, and Enter handoff to the Timeline. change-inspector-interaction.ts owns the local Change and Timeline cursors, Change-first shortcuts, its palette/help dialogs, reader-local display controls, and route-transition focus entry/restoration after each DOM paint. change-inspector-timeline-navigation.ts owns pure page-local Timeline cursor intent, while change-inspector-timeline-boundary.ts owns opaque signed-continuation traversal to global boundaries. On an exact-event route that Timeline cursor drives its own event route through replace, so the open detail, the address bar, and the cursor always name the same event; cursor-driven selection scrolls the row into view without focusing the Timeline, and the exact-activation focus repair fires for a followed route only to return focus the repaint itself destroyed. auth.ts separately owns reconnect-dialog settlement, its focus trap, and focus restoration so authentication cannot be hidden while its request remains pending. change-inspector-render.ts owns focusable Change/Revision reading controls plus exact fact/file anchor focus inside the projected detail. change-inspector-graphs.ts owns keyboard activation of server-laid relationship nodes and emits only explicit exact-identity callbacks. change-inspector-diff.ts owns full-frame file/fact navigation and deep-link focus inside one contextual exact Revision; change-inspector-interaction.ts owns the visible focus handoff into and out of that route. Legacy keyboard, palette, detail, diff-controller, render, and main modules remain outside that composition until each is explicitly adapted with Change-first tests.

modules.reason: Owns capability recovery and the reconnect dialog's settlement, focus trap, and focus restoration. The Change-first interaction controller deliberately does not hide or settle that auth-owned dialog.
Contains argument-driven fact-card HTML emitters used only beneath exact Revision resources. It owns no selection, transport, aggregate store, or Change membership semantics.
Derives removable structured-query chips from the shared parser and raw token indexes. It is argument-driven and cannot read routes, state, transport, or Change membership.
Maps server-owned Change summaries and exact Revision pairs to accessible card presentation without inventing a title, choosing a current Revision, or deriving Change semantics in the browser.

Owns the full-frame Change-aware annotated diff. It consumes only an already validated contextual exact-Revision document, adapts its exact fact presentations to the model-neutral diff renderer, and keeps file/fact/search deep links as route intent. It imports neither the legacy aggregate store nor the quarantined diff controller.

Maps one already-decoded typed Timeline event to stable labels, actor/track metadata, colors, and detail rows. It is argument-driven, has no transport or state, and cannot derive Change membership or select a Revision.

Paints only server-laid Change and fact relationship geometry, preserves effective topology separately from unresolved claims and each fact-edge family separately, and emits exact identity callbacks without deriving a winner or importing legacy aggregate state.
Owns authenticated transport for the bounded Change reader and path-private identity document, plus typed request failures. It cannot construct or call legacy aggregate-reader routes.
Strictly decodes the path-private repository, store, family, and worktree identity used by active session chrome. It owns no semantic generation, route, or transport state.
Owns Change-first keyboard, route focus, palette/help dialogs, split, reading-mode, theme, density, and page-local Timeline cursor behavior. Its local cursors never choose a Revision implicitly.
Builds the shared accessible heading and compact metadata pair for an already selected lens. It owns no route, state, transport, or Change semantics.
Loads only typed Change detail, exact Revision detail/resource, association, and interdiff documents through versioned Change-reader routes and keeps each exact identity distinct.

Owns the active search draft, bounded replace cadence, accessible completion list, and parser diagnostics. It consumes only accepted Event History completion values and callback-owned route intent, without fetching or constructing exact semantic routes.
Projects one accepted Change-reader snapshot into the active shell, filters, Change cards, exact Revision reading surfaces, and Timeline detail. It fetches nothing and owns no semantic state.
Owns Change-first fragments and bounded query syntax, including exact event routes and exact Revision pairs. URL state is request intent, never browser-derived Change state.
Owns the profile-to-staged-generation-to-route-to-paint state machine and refuses incoherent stamps. It preserves explicit Change and exact Revision selections across accepted generations.

Owns honest global Timeline boundary traversal. It starts from a filtered first page, follows only opaque signed continuations from one immutable generation, detects refusal/no-progress, and returns a bounded route without owning DOM or history.
Owns session-only follow, park, and new-event counts for an eligible Timeline head. It never reorders entries, decodes continuations, or replaces a parked window without explicit reader action.
Owns the pure page-local Timeline selection model for j/k, page movement, and local boundaries. It emits adjacent-page intent at a real page edge and never infers an unmaterialized event.

Projects only the typed paged `/api/v2/history` document into a page-local virtualized Timeline. It preserves server-owned chronology and offers Change context only through explicit Change or exact Revision routes; it imports neither the legacy aggregate store nor legacy history endpoints.

Is the sole served Change-first composition root. It owns request epochs, profile preflight/postflight, one staged generation, route resolution, Timeline monitoring and boundary traversal, then delegates a coherent snapshot for paint.
Defines and validates the versioned Change-reader wire contract, exact Revision pairs, Timeline documents, authority cursor, projection stamps, and reader-profile invariants.
Owns only local connection and refresh presentation state plus reconnect/retry controls. It cannot fetch data or interpret Change, Revision, or Timeline semantics.
Reads the legacy selected-event/revision aggregate store and fetches legacy revision composites. Exact Change/Revision detail now comes only from change-inspector-reading.ts.
Its route, selection, and snapshot lifecycle are coupled to the legacy aggregate store. The active reader renders only an exact captured resource validated by the Change-first protocol.
Provides a pure fail-safe attributed-segment renderer for exact diff rows. It has no DOM, state, transport, identity selection, or Change semantics.
Provides argument-driven exact diff, file, and annotation rendering beneath a validated Revision resource. The stateful legacy diff controller remains quarantined.
Owns only anchored panel visibility, aria-expanded state, dismissal, and focus return for filter/view controls; it has no review-model or routing authority.
Is the served bootstrap leaf and imports only change-inspector.ts. Keeping it in the inventory makes the complete active TypeScript closure auditable from its actual root.
Its global shortcuts advance legacy aggregate Timeline/Revision cursors. Change-aware Timeline, Change, and exact-Revision keyboard behavior lives in change-inspector-interaction.ts instead.
Legacy aggregate composition root retained solely for its isolated historical tests; entry.ts is the sole served Change-first composition root.
Provides pure escaped body rendering for server-provided content types. It owns no selection, transport, aggregate state, or Change inference.
Its command set targets legacy entity, lens, and selection state. It may be adapted only after Change-first command and focus contracts exist.
Theme, density, and split are reader-local display preferences; they neither fetch nor infer review semantics. Active composition may import only this model-neutral preference surface.
Contains argument-driven fact and entry display helpers reused only beneath exact server-owned documents. It does not read the legacy store or resolve Change membership.
Retains the pure bounded query grammar used within exact diff and card presentation. Timeline filtering remains server-owned and this helper cannot fetch or widen a result set.
Provides pure reference classification, safe linkification, and display short forms. It has no route, selection, store, or Change membership authority.
The legacy store subscriber paints aggregate Timeline and Revision semantics. change-inspector-render.ts is the active bounded projection renderer.
Paints only server-computed, node-id-agnostic supersession geometry supplied to an exact fact card. It never computes topology or chooses a Revision.
Defines only server-provided supersession graph geometry. Both retained legacy readers and active Change-first fact cards may consume this neutral wire contract without reaching the aggregate store.
Provides shared pure view constants and structural types consumed by retained exact-resource renderers. It owns no state, transport, route, or Change/Revision resolution.
